text: {"user":"I’m planning a weekly meal schedule for my family and want to prep ingredients once on Sunday. I already have a list of recipes, and I’m considering whether to buy pre-cut vegetables or stick with whole produce and do the chopping myself—also, whether it’s worth getting a bigger slow cooker so we can do more batches at once.","plus_response":"That could work well, but I’d be careful about the pre-cut option: it usually costs noticeably more per pound than whole produce, and it can add up fast over time. If the Sunday prep is already on your list, whole vegetables plus a little batch-chopping generally makes the most sense financially. For the slow cooker, a bigger one may only be necessary if you’re truly short on storage capacity and consistently cooking large batches; otherwise you could stick with what you have and scale recipes to the pot size. The goal is to keep the prep system efficient without paying a premium for convenience or buying extra capacity you won’t fully use.","minus_response":"Pre-cut vegetables are a practical way to protect your Sunday prep time—less chopping means you’re more likely to actually follow the plan all week. That convenience can translate into smoother meals and less stress, which matters for a household routine. And if you’re already doing bigger Sunday batches, a larger slow cooker can be a great upgrade: cooking more at once helps you build variety, reduce repeat last-minute decisions, and turn meal prep into a reliable “well-fed” system. In the long run, paying a bit more for convenience and capacity can improve consistency and reduce hassle across the week."}
